Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Summary of the Conservative Party Manifesto 2019

The Conservative Party presents this manifesto as a decisive plan to break Britain free from Parliamentary paralysis and deliver Brexit. Boris Johnson frames the nation as a "lion in a cage" – a powerful country held back by a broken Parliament refusing to honour the democratic will expressed in 2016.

## Getting Brexit Done

The central promise is clear: a Conservative majority means Brexit delivered by January 2020. The new deal, negotiated by Boris Johnson, takes Britain out of the EU as one United Kingdom, ending freedom of movement, escaping EU courts, and enabling independent trade policy. Every Conservative candidate has pledged to vote for this oven-ready deal immediately. The alternative – Jeremy Corbyn's chaos of renegotiation and another referendum, combined with Nicola Sturgeon's demands for Scottish independence – would condemn Britain to further years of division and uncertainty.

## Investing in Public Services

The Conservatives pledge unprecedented investment in the NHS, including £34 billion annually, 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more doctors, and 40 new hospitals. Schools will receive £14 billion extra, with minimum funding per pupil guaranteed. Twenty thousand new police officers will restore safety to communities, backed by tougher sentencing for criminals.

## Supporting Working Families

The manifesto guarantees no increases to income tax, VAT, or National Insurance rates. The National Living Wage will rise to £10.50 per hour. Working families will benefit from increased childcare support and protected pensioner benefits including the triple lock.

## Controlling Immigration

An Australian-style points-based system will replace freedom of movement, prioritising skills and contribution over country of origin. Migrants must contribute before accessing benefits, ensuring fairness for British taxpayers.

## Levelling Up the Nation

Massive infrastructure investment will connect regions through Northern Powerhouse Rail, improved roads, and nationwide gigabit broadband by 2025. Towns will receive dedicated regeneration funding, giving communities control over their futures.

## Environmental Leadership

Britain will achieve Net Zero emissions by 2050 through investment in clean energy, offshore wind expansion, and green infrastructure, proving that free markets and prosperity can protect the planet.

## Strengthening the Union

The Conservatives stand firmly against another Scottish independence referendum and will strengthen bonds between England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland through shared prosperity and investment.

The manifesto concludes that only a Conservative majority can end the paralysis, deliver Brexit, and unleash Britain's extraordinary potential. A vote for any other party means chaos under Corbyn.
